title: The 6 Best ConductorOne Alternatives in 2026 | Features, Pricing & Buyer Guide
summary: Compare 6 ConductorOne (C1) alternatives for 2026: AccessOwl, SailPoint, Torii, JumpCloud, Entra ID Governance and Multiplier. Provisioning, Okta fit, pricing.
body_markdown:
ConductorOne (now C1) tends to land at companies with a mature identity stack, where Okta is the identity provider, most apps have SCIM and SAML switched on, and a security team owns access. C1 then adds governance on top: access reviews, policy and just-in-time access.


But many growing companies simply want onboarding, offboarding and access reviews automated before they have that complex setup.


> "Our team bought Conductor One believing it could do the whole lifecycle provisioning, because it's advertised like it can. It does not. They have maybe 50 to 80 pre-built connectors. The vast majority of their connectors do not have account provisioning or deprovisioning components built out."
>
>
> IAM engineer at a fast-growing, 120-person developer platform


This guide covers six C1 alternatives. We based it on our own research and on conversations with 450+ IT buyers who evaluated access management tools, some of whom assessed or used C1. For a direct comparison, read our[ConductorOne vs AccessOwl page](https://www.accessowl.com/alternatives/conductorone-vs-accessowl) .


## TL;DR


C1 does identity governance well, especially access reviews and policy. Whether it can create and remove accounts depends on each connector, and it works best once Okta and SCIM are in place across your stack. The best alternative for you depends on how much of that stack you have today.


-


AccessOwl is the best alternative for teams of 30 to 1,000 people that want access automation running across all their SaaS apps first, without standing up a large governance program.


-


SailPoint is the incumbent for large enterprises with an identity team and complex, regulated systems.


-


Torii is the pick if what you really need is SaaS spend management.


-


JumpCloud suits small IT teams that want a directory, SSO and device management from one vendor.


-


Multiplier is a smaller pick for teams that already run IT requests through Jira Service Management.


## ConductorOne (C1) is being acquired by Workday


In October 2026, Workday signed an agreement to acquire C1. Workday wants C1 to become the identity governance layer next to its HR and finance systems. The deal is expected to close by the end of January 2027.


C1 already leaned on Okta, SCIM and enterprise-tier app plans. As part of Workday, its roadmap will likely follow Workday's large enterprise customers. If you're considering alternatives to C1 after the news, AccessOwl is a fit for companies with 30 to 1,000 employees. AccessOwl works with 50+ HR systems and is built for teams on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365. It automates access in 500+ apps, with no SCIM tax.


## Why teams move away from ConductorOne


C1 is open about its target buyer. Its website talks to security teams, IAM engineers and risk and compliance leaders. A typical C1 customer has a security team, runs Okta and has budget set aside for a governance program. Buyers we talked to who were missing one of those ran into the same three problems.


### JML automation comes second to governance in C1


What C1 does best is governance: access reviews, policy, entitlements and just-in-time access. Creating and deleting accounts when people join, move or leave is a separate job. Whether C1 can do it depends on the connector.


The numbers in C1's own docs show the split. Its catalog lists 455 apps. Of the 392 connectors with a capability table, about 118 can create accounts, and about 222 only sync data for reviews. For every other app, someone still has to add or remove the account.


AccessOwl supports provisioning and deprovisioning in every one of the[496 SaaS apps in our catalog](https://www.accessowl.com/integrations) .


### C1 assumes an Okta foundation


C1 sits on top of your identity provider. It connects to Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace and others. When a C1 connector can't create an account, it hands the job back to the identity provider, usually through group membership. In practice that means Okta, with SCIM configured for each app.


On Google Workspace, that fallback covers less than you might expect. Google Workspace automates provisioning for a set list of about 57 apps, and the apps your leavers use may not be on it. In our[State of SaaS Access Management 2026](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/state-of-saas-access-management-2026) data, a leaver had to be removed from a median of 17 apps beyond Google or Microsoft, held by 8 different app admins. Our comparison of[offboarding automation tools](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/best-tools-automating-offboarding-access-revocation) shows how many of those apps each tool can actually deprovision.


The buyers we talked to who picked C1 fit that pattern. They had moved every app onto Okta, wanted governance on top of it and had a security or identity team to run it.


AccessOwl works on top of Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 as you run them today. It works with Okta too.


### C1 costs an enterprise budget, before the SSO tax


C1 doesn't list prices on its website. Its[AWS Marketplace listing](https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/pp/prodview-wrixbdsadifke) shows $100,000 for 12 months. An IT lead at a European fintech with about 650 users compared C1 and Lumos and told us:


> "The first tools we looked at were Conductor One and Lumos. I liked the product itself. But they were super, super expensive for us. They quoted me something around 80k. That's out of the budget constraints we have."
>
>
> IT lead at a European fintech with about 650 users


The license is only one line in the budget. Many C1 connectors provision through an app's SCIM or admin API, and SaaS vendors tend to reserve those for their enterprise plans. That's the[SSO tax](https://www.ssotax.org/) . C1's Slack docs say automatic account provisioning "is not currently supported for Slack Pro workspaces." Its Notion connector doesn't work "with the Free, Plus, or Business editions of Notion."


AccessOwl connects through an integration account on the plan you already have, with no SCIM needed. For example,[AccessOwl provisions Slack on any paid plan](https://www.accessowl.com/integrations/slack) .


## Criteria when comparing ConductorOne alternatives


We compared these tools on the questions buyers ask us most often, not on feature counts:


-


Fit with your current stack: Does it work with the identity setup you already run, or does it expect Okta and SCIM everywhere?


-


Accounts, not just reviews: How many apps can it create and remove accounts in without custom work?


-


SSO and SCIM tax: Will you need to move apps onto enterprise plans before it can automate them?


-


Time to value: How fast do onboarding and offboarding start running on their own, and who has to run it?


-


Pricing: Is the price on the website, or do you need a sales call to find it?


## AccessOwl: The Best ConductorOne Alternative for IGA Across SaaS Apps


AccessOwl is the strongest choice if you want access automation working across every SaaS app you use, without first standing up a large governance program. C1 governs what its connectors can reach and passes the rest to your identity provider or a person. AccessOwl creates, reviews and removes access inside each app. It's built for the IT team, or whoever handles IT alongside their main job, who wants access handled automatically from hire to exit.


Most companies have far more apps than anyone governs. In our[State of SaaS Access Management 2026](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/state-of-saas-access-management-2026) report, only about 3 in 10 apps employees signed into were managed. At the median company, employees signed into or connected about 110 apps, and only about 35 of them were managed.


### What AccessOwl does


-


**New hires are ready on day one:** A start date in your HR system creates accounts in each app with the right role, groups and workspaces. Nobody logs into admin consoles to set them up.


-


**Leavers lose access on schedule:** After the last workday, AccessOwl removes accounts in every connected app, frees the licenses and logs each step. Apps outside SSO are flagged for review.


-


**Access requests in minutes, not days:** Employees pick the app and access level they need. Managers approve in one click, and AccessOwl sets up the account without anyone opening an admin console.


-


**Temporary access ends on time:** Grant access for a set period, like a short project or a few days on a sensitive system. AccessOwl removes it inside the app when the period ends, so nobody has to remember.


-


**Access reviews in about 15 minutes per app:** Managers review their team's access in one place, with context like role, department and how access was granted. Compliance owners spend about 15 minutes per app instead of hours, and the evidence is ready for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 auditors.


-


**No enterprise plan upgrades:** Most apps connect through an integration account, so you don't buy an app's enterprise plan to automate it. All[496 SaaS apps in our catalog](https://www.accessowl.com/integrations) support provisioning and deprovisioning. APIs and SCIM are also supported.


Teams on Slack request access with /request and approve in the same thread, using our[native Slack app](https://www.accessowl.com/slack) . Teams that don't use Slack request and approve in the web dashboard. You can also connect AccessOwl to your own tools through its API and MCP.


Motion, a 20-person AI software company, used AccessOwl before it had an IT department. Their cofounder told us what changed:


> "Onboarding probably went from two hours down to less than half an hour."
>
>
> Ethan Yu, Cofounder & COO, from[Motion's success story](https://www.accessowl.com/customers/motion)


### Who AccessOwl is a fit for


AccessOwl is built for companies of about 30 to 1,000 people. C1 gets the most out of a setup where Okta, SCIM and a security team are already in place. AccessOwl works with the setup you have now, before there's a formal identity governance program.


Who runs it differs from company to company. It might be a solo IT admin or a small IT team. Often it's a senior HR or Ops lead who owns onboarding and offboarding and wants them to run without constant follow-up.


AccessOwl doesn't provide SSO or MFA. Sign-in stays with Google Workspace, Microsoft or your identity provider.


### Why AccessOwl is best for companies under 1,000 employees


**Live in one day:** Connect Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 in a few clicks, add your apps, and turn on the workflows you need. There's no migration and no identity project to finish first.


**Public pricing.**[AccessOwl's prices are on the website](https://www.accessowl.com/pricing) . Plans start at $250 a month, and there's a 7-day free trial, so you know the cost before any sales call.


**Spend tracking included.** AccessOwl also tracks app costs and renewals, and finds shadow apps from Google and Microsoft sign-ins.


**Made for Google Workspace and Microsoft 365.** AccessOwl sits on top of[Google Workspace](https://www.accessowl.com/google-workspace) or[Microsoft 365](https://www.accessowl.com/microsoft-365) and connects in minutes, with no migration. It also integrates with identity providers like Okta and with 50+ HR systems, so joiners and leavers come from data you already keep.


**Ready for AI assistants.** Besides its API and MCP, AccessOwl ships premade[AccessOwl skills](https://docs.accessowl.com/guides/ai/accessowl-skills) for assistants like Claude and Codex. IT can ask the assistant to onboard someone, see what a person can access or schedule an offboarding. The assistant can't approve anything. Every request still goes through your approval rules.


### Bottom line


If you're leaving C1 because you want access automation working now, not a large governance program first, AccessOwl runs onboarding, offboarding, requests and reviews across 500+ apps without SCIM or enterprise plan upgrades. It works on top of Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 and shows its prices up front. Teams under 1,000 people usually go live within days.

## SailPoint (best for large enterprises with a mature identity program)


SailPoint is the incumbent in identity governance, and it says 54% of the Fortune 500 are customers. Buyers often weigh C1 against SailPoint, since C1 pitches itself as a newer take on what SailPoint has long done for large enterprises. SailPoint runs as a cloud platform, or self-hosted for companies that need governance on their own infrastructure.


### What SailPoint offers


-


Joiner, mover and leaver workflows driven by your HR system.


-


Access certifications and reviews, plus role modeling to bundle access into roles.


-


Separation-of-duties checks, through an Access Risk Management add-on.


-


Just-in-time access for elevated permissions on its Business suites.


-


Hundreds of connectors, including on-premises systems like Active Directory and ERP platforms.


-


SaaS discovery through a browser extension and SSO connectors.


-


Governance for AI agents and machine identities, launched as Agentic Fabric in 2026.


### Where it falls short


SailPoint is built and priced for large enterprises. It doesn't publish prices.[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/sailpoint) puts the median buyer at about $110,000 a year, based on 39 purchases, and notes that professional services commonly add 30 to 50% in the first year.


Accounts are created through connectors. SailPoint's SCIM connector requires a virtual appliance to be set up first, and it can only provision apps that offer SCIM on the plan you pay for. For the long tail of SaaS apps, the SSO tax comes back.


Getting it live is a project. SailPoint doesn't publish a typical timeline. Its Standard suite, aimed at companies "early in their identity security journey", came with a services package promising a return on investment in 8 to 12 weeks. Most rollouts are run by an identity team, often with an implementation partner.


### Where it fits


SailPoint fits a large enterprise with an identity team, strict audit requirements and a mix of cloud, on-premises and ERP systems to govern. If you're moving off C1 because you need more governance depth at enterprise scale, SailPoint is the established option.


## Torii (best if SaaS spend management is the main job)


Torii is a SaaS management platform that started with spend. It discovers the apps people use, shows what you pay for them and helps you cut the ones you don't need. Its shadow IT detection, spend dashboards and contract tracking are some of the best on the market. In October 2026, Freshworks agreed to acquire Torii and fold it into Freshservice.


### Where it fits


Torii fits companies where Finance drives the purchase and the goal is to see and reduce SaaS spend. If you were looking at C1 mostly to get visibility into your app spend, Torii does that well.


### Where it falls short


Access came later in Torii, and provisioning depends on each app's API. Of the 298 apps in its integration directory, 105 list actions to both create and remove a user. By default, an approved access request sends an email to the app owner. The account is only created or removed automatically if you build an API workflow for that app. Torii doesn't publish pricing.[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/torii) puts the median buyer at about $32,000 a year.


### Bottom line


Torii is a good fit when spend is the job and Finance owns it. If access is the job, our[Torii comparison](https://www.accessowl.com/alternatives/torii-vs-accessowl) covers the differences.


## JumpCloud (best for small IT teams that want directory, SSO and device management in one)


JumpCloud puts a cloud directory, SSO, MFA and device management in a single platform. It manages Windows, Mac, Linux, iOS and Android devices. Device management is something no other tool on this list does. Over the past year it has added SaaS discovery, access requests and, in November 2026, access certifications.


### Where it fits


JumpCloud fits small and mid-sized IT teams that want one vendor for sign-in and devices, especially with a mix of Mac and Windows laptops. Its pricing is public. Device Management starts at $9 per user a month and SSO at $11 per user a month, billed annually.[Vendr's data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/jumpcloud) puts the median buyer at about $40,000 a year.


### Where it falls short


JumpCloud creates accounts in SaaS apps through SCIM, so apps that keep SCIM on their enterprise plan still carry the SSO tax. Access requests and access certifications are new. They're sold as a $5 per user a month add-on unless you're on the top Platform Prime plan.


### Bottom line


JumpCloud makes sense if you want a directory, SSO and devices from one vendor. If governing access across all your SaaS apps is the goal, check which of your apps it can provision before you commit.


## Microsoft Entra ID Governance (best for teams that run everything on Microsoft)


If you're on Microsoft 365, part of what C1 does may already be available to you. Microsoft Entra ID Governance is an add-on that sits on top of Entra ID P1 or P2. It brings access reviews, lifecycle workflows for joiners, movers and leavers, and access packages that employees request with approvals and expiry dates.


### Where it fits


Entra ID Governance fits teams that run everything on Microsoft and whose apps mostly support SCIM on the plan they pay for. In that setup, Microsoft's own tools may cover what you need.


### Where it falls short


Entra provisions apps through SCIM. If an app has no SCIM endpoint on your plan, Entra can't create, remove or review its accounts. Buyers also find the licensing confusing, since P1, P2 and the Governance add-on each unlock different features. Our guide to[Entra ID SCIM provisioning limitations](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/entra-id-scim-provisioning-limitations) shows where Entra stops.


### Bottom line


Entra ID Governance works well when Microsoft covers most of your stack. For everything outside it, see our roundup of the[best Entra ID Governance alternatives](https://www.accessowl.com/blog/entra-id-governance-alternatives) .


## Multiplier (a smaller pick for teams on Jira Service Management)


Multiplier is a smaller, lesser-known tool built for one kind of team: IT teams that already run their requests through Jira Service Management. It describes itself as an "Identity Governance and Access Management Platform for Jira". Access requests, approvals and access reviews all happen in Jira, with Slack as a second place to request access.


### What Multiplier offers


-


An app catalog in the Jira Service Management portal, with manager and app owner approvals.


-


Time-limited access to apps, groups and roles.


-


Onboarding, role change and offboarding workflows from a no-code builder.


-


Access review campaigns run in Jira, with revoked access removed and logged.


-


Connections to Okta, Microsoft Entra, Google Workspace and JumpCloud.


### Where it fits


Multiplier fits companies where IT already lives in Jira Service Management and wants access requests and reviews in the same place. Its pricing is public. Standard costs $5 per user a month and Advanced $6, with a 30-day free trial.


### Where it falls short


Multiplier is tied to Jira. It's billed through Atlassian for every licensed Jira user in your site, and you can't license only part of your Jira users. If your company doesn't run on Jira Service Management, it isn't built for you. Provisioning runs through your identity provider, so the apps it can automate depend on what your identity provider can provision. That often means SCIM on each app's enterprise plan.


### Bottom line


Multiplier is a good fit for a Jira-first IT team that wants access requests and reviews in its service desk. If you need accounts created in apps your identity provider can't reach, check coverage app by app.


## How to choose the right ConductorOne alternative


-


Is Okta your core identity provider today, or are you on Google Workspace or Microsoft 365?


-


Which of your apps will the tool create and remove accounts in, and which will turn into a task for someone?


-


How many of those apps would need an enterprise plan before the tool can automate them?


-


Can you test the tool on all of your apps before you sign?


-


Do you need an enterprise governance program, or do you need access automated in the stack you have today?

## FAQs


### What is the best alternative to ConductorOne?


That depends on your stack. For companies of 30 to 1,000 people who want access automation without a large governance program, AccessOwl automates onboarding, offboarding, requests and access reviews in 500+ apps without SCIM. Large enterprises with an identity team usually look at SailPoint. Teams on Microsoft can start with Entra ID Governance, and Jira-first IT teams can look at Multiplier.


### Is SailPoint a good alternative to ConductorOne?


For large enterprises, yes. SailPoint is the established identity governance platform, with deep lifecycle, certification and separation-of-duties features and connectors for on-premises systems. It's priced and rolled out like enterprise software. Vendr puts the median buyer at about $110,000 a year, and an identity team usually runs the rollout with a services partner.


### What happens to ConductorOne after the Workday acquisition?


Workday signed an agreement to acquire C1 in October 2026, and the deal is expected to close by the end of January 2027. Workday plans to make C1 the identity governance layer next to its HR and finance systems. Acquisitions often lead to changes in pricing, packaging and roadmap, so review your contract before it renews.


### Which ConductorOne alternatives have public pricing?


AccessOwl, JumpCloud and Multiplier show their prices. AccessOwl starts at $250 a month with a 7-day free trial. JumpCloud starts at $9 per user a month for device management. Multiplier starts at $5 per Jira user a month. SailPoint and Torii are sales-gated.


### Do I need Okta to use AccessOwl?


No. AccessOwl works on top of Google Workspace or Microsoft 365, and it also connects to Okta. It creates and removes accounts through integration accounts, so it doesn't need SCIM set up for each app.
